claims.text: Protective-scale formation and persistence above 900 °C are governed by the oxidation kinetics of X relative to Cr and by oxide/substrate lattice and thermal-expansion compatibility.
Al-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys form alumina-containing surface oxides.
Si-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys form silicate surface phases.
Al- and Si-derived oxides grow more slowly than the oxide on the Mn-containing alloy.
Al- and Si-derived oxides have better crystallographic alignment with the substrate than Mn-derived oxides.
Al- and Si-derived oxides have better thermal-expansion compatibility with the substrate than Mn-derived oxides.
Slower oxide growth and improved lattice and thermal compatibility reduce stress accumulation during growth and thermal cycling.
The Mn-containing alloy typically forms a mixed Mn-oxide scale.
The Mn-containing alloy develops a faster-growing oxide than the Al- and Si-containing alloys.
Poorer lattice and thermal-expansion matching in the Mn-containing alloy generates greater interfacial tensile stress.
Greater oxide-scale tensile stress promotes cracking and spallation.
Al- and Si-containing alloys form continuous, adherent scales that thicken by diffusion-limited processes.
Relative to CrFeCoNiMn, the Al- and Si-containing alloys will have more continuous and coherent scales with less cracking and spallation during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
CrFeCoNiMn will form a less adherent and less protective oxide scale because of faster oxidation and greater oxide/substrate mechanical mismatch.
The proposed comparison controls processing by preparing the Al-, Si-, and Mn-containing alloys under identical melting, homogenization, and thermomechanical conditions.
The proposed hypothesis applies to single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution CrFeCoNiX alloys exposed above 900 °C for extended durations in oxidative or corrosive atmospheres.
Processing and microstructural variations may alter the contribution of each alloying element to oxidation behavior.
Comparable or greater cracking or spallation in the Al- or Si-containing alloy than in CrFeCoNiMn under the same exposure would falsify the predicted ranking.
Failure of lattice or thermal-expansion compatibility to correlate with oxide stability would challenge the proposed mechanism.
